name: io.github.qxxx5vyd77-byte/directors-lookbook
title: Director's Lookbook
description: 790+ named visual and music styles: deal a look for a feeling, get paste-ready AI prompts.

tools.name: find_styles
tools.description: Search the 840 cards by feeling, mood, era, technique or style name. Use it when someone names or describes a specific look, lens, film stock, light, palette, font or music style ("what does Portra 400 look like", "ring light macro", "Wes Anderson-style symmetry" finds Planimetric Tableau), to identify a named look ("Kodak Gold" finds Gold 200), to find a replacement for one card in a hand, or to browse one suit. Examples: {"query": "film noir"}, {"query": "90s camcorder"}, {"query": "cozy rainy", "suit": "color"}, {"query": "bossa nova", "suit": "score", "top": 3}. Returns ranked cards (id, suit, kind, name, what, example image). When nothing matches directly it says so and returns related styles or did-you-mean suggestions. For a full matched set of cards for a project use deal_hand instead.

query.description: A feeling, mood, era, technique or style name, e.g. "dreamy 70s summer", "anamorphic", "risograph", "lo-fi beats". Words after "no"/"not" count against a card.

suit.description: Optional filter. type = typefaces, camera = shots, moves, lenses and lighting, film = looks and mediums, color = palettes and grades, score = music styles, web = site motion and layout.

tools.name: deal_hand
tools.description: Start here whenever someone asks for an image, video or music prompt, a photo or film look, or art direction from a description ("a moody product shot of perfume", "rainy cafe at night", "a Suno style for a sad song"): deal one matched card per slot for the job from their plain-language feeling. photo = one image (film, camera, color, light); still = image with title type; cover = album or poster art (film, color, type); video or reel = clip or short (film, camera, color, type, score, light); lyric = lyric video (same as reel); song = music only (score); site = website (film, color, type, web); game = key art, store capsule, sprites, UI and loop music (film, color, type, score); drama = a short drama ad where the ad is the show (film, camera, color, type, score, light, and three shots: hook, twist, payoff); all = every suit. Example: {"feeling": "lonely astronaut on a desert planet at dusk", "job": "video", "shots": 3}. Same seed + same inputs = same hand; a new seed re-deals; hold keeps chosen cards ({"film": "film-gold-200"}). For job drama the hand also carries three shots (hook close-up, twist reveal, payoff wide or push) and the look is dealt from the feeling, with the subject read as the product. Returns the hand (slot to card id and name), the main paste-ready prompt for the job (prompt), why each card was picked, clashes, and a site_url showing the hand with pictures. Show the user the prompt and the site_url; use brief with the hand ids for every block (shot lists, palette, Suno, Midjourney spelling).

feeling.description: The feeling or scene in plain words, e.g. "rainy cafe at night, melancholy". Words after "no"/"not" count against a card. For drama, the story's feeling or situation, e.g. "a quiet breakup at a dinner table".

job.description: What the hand is for (default photo); see the job list above.

seed.description: Optional integer for a repeatable deal. Omit for a fresh random deal.

hold.description: Optional cards to keep, as {slot: card id}, e.g. {"film": "film-gold-200", "score": "score-bossa-nova"}. Slots: type, camera, film, color, score, web, light.

subject.description: Optional subject, e.g. "a jazz singer". It is folded into the feeling so scene and person words count. For drama, the product being advertised (used for the setting check, not for picking the look).

aspect.description: Optional frame for the clash check, e.g. "2.39:1" for a film or "9:16" for a reel (default 9:16 for reel and lyric). Pass the same aspect to brief.

shots.description: Optional, for video, reel, lyric or all: also pick a shot list of this many camera cards (the dealt camera first, then matched shots and moves). Pass them all to brief to get one SHOT block each. A drama hand always has 3 (hook, twist, payoff).

moods.description: Optional mood chips that weigh more than words. One or more of: cozy, eerie, nostalgic, epic, playful, tense, dreamy, gritty, elegant, kinetic, melancholy, hopeful, futuristic, handmade, serene, bold.

tools.name: brief
tools.description: Turn card ids into paste-ready prompt blocks, worded verbatim from the cards: IMAGE PROMPT, VIDEO PROMPT, PALETTE (hexes), TYPE, SUNO STYLE and SUNO EXCLUDE, SITE PROMPT, or for job game: KEY ART, CAPSULE, SPRITE/TILESET, UI MOCKUP, MUSIC; for job drama: SHOT blocks for the hook, twist and payoff plus BEATS (timing, shot, what happens, a placeholder line with its length rule), END CARD (title, promise, call to action, set in the type card), CAPTION RULES (safe band y 210 to 1345 on 1080x1920, nothing in the bottom 30%) and DON'T. Pass the ids from deal_hand (or find_styles), at most one card per suit, except camera: several camera cards make a shot list (one SHOT block each). A camera card of kind light lights every shot; a film card of kind fx adds a post effect. tool respells the blocks: midjourney (--ar, --style raw, --sref with the film card's example image), runway or kling (camera line first, 5 or 10 s clips), suno (music blocks only). seconds splits a running time over the shots, beats says what happens in each, vocals picks lyrics or instrumental. A lens card in a shot list shapes every shot. Example: {"hand_ids": ["film-gold-200", "camera-closeup", "color-golden-hour"], "job": "photo", "subject": "an older woman teaching a young man to dance", "tool": "midjourney"}. Drama example: {"hand_ids": ["type-futura", "film-vision3-500t", "color-blue-hour", "camera-closeup", "camera-pull", "camera-push"], "job": "drama", "subject": "a meal-kit app", "feeling": "a quiet breakup at a dinner table", "title": "Dinner for Two", "seconds": 30}. Also returns the don't-list, tone words, deliverables, lint warnings and a site_url.

hand_ids.description: Card ids from deal_hand or find_styles, e.g. ["film-gold-200", "camera-closeup", "color-golden-hour"]. One per suit, except several camera cards = a shot list.

job.description: What the brief is for (default reel); use the job you dealt for. photo = a still image, video = reel, song = Suno blocks only, site = SITE PROMPT, game = key art set, drama = short drama ad (beats, end card, caption rules).

subject.description: Who or what is in the shot, e.g. "a lighthouse keeper on a rocky coast". Without it the prompts say [your subject]. For drama, the product being advertised.

title.description: Optional title lettering for the image or key art (set in the type card). For drama, the show or brand name on the end card.

feeling.description: Drama only: the story's feeling or situation, e.g. "a quiet breakup at a dinner table". The hook opens on it and every shot carries it.

aspect.description: Optional aspect ratio, e.g. "16:9", "9:16", "4:5", "1:1", "2.39:1". Default 9:16 for reel and lyric, 16:9 for game.

tool.description: Target tool: any (plain prose), midjourney, runway or kling (camera line first, shots capped at 10 s), suno (music blocks only), openfilm (leads with a FILM PLAN and a LOOK.CSS for a coding agent building the film as web pages in OpenFilm).

beats.description: Optional: what happens in each shot, in order, e.g. ["they sit in silence", "she slides a photo across the table"]. Beat n goes into SHOT n (or the one VIDEO PROMPT).

vocals.description: Optional for music: "lyrics" lifts vocal bans out of SUNO EXCLUDE so a sung track can exist; "instrumental" adds them.

seconds.description: Optional running time in seconds, e.g. 15 for a reel or 60 for a short: split across the SHOT blocks (or the one VIDEO PROMPT) as "Duration: N s." Drama: 15 to 60, default 30, timed hook, twist, payoff.

tools.name: show_card
tools.description: One card in full: what it is, the prompt wording ("ask"), what not to do, feels, moods, pairs, swatch hexes or font details, plus image, clip and music_sample URLs when it has them. Example: {"id": "film-gold-200"}. A wrong id returns did-you-mean suggestions.

id.description: Card id from find_styles or deal_hand, e.g. "film-gold-200", "camera-dutch", "score-bossa-nova".

tools.name: list_suits
tools.description: Card counts per suit and per kind (for example camera: shot, move, lens, light). Use it to see what the lookbook covers before searching.

tools.name: lint_hand
tools.description: Check card ids you combined yourself for clashes before briefing: black-and-white film with a colour grade, two grades stacked, daylight with a night palette, an anamorphic lens in a vertical frame, an interior light with an outdoor subject. Example: {"hand_ids": ["film-pushed-bw-1600", "color-teal-orange"], "aspect": "9:16"}. ok: true means clean. deal_hand and brief already lint their own output.

subject.description: Optional subject; enables the light-vs-setting check.
